subject: maths
question: If sqrt{3} tan θ = 3 sin θ, then what is the value of sin² θ − cos² θ ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

√3 tan θ = 3 sin θ ⇒ √3 (sin θ / cos θ) = 3 sin θ

Canceling sin θ on both sides: √3 / cos θ = 3 ⇒ cos θ = √3 / 3 = 1 / √3

Then, cos² θ = 1 / 3

Expression: sin² θ − cos² θ = (1 − cos² θ) − cos² θ = 1 − 2 cos² θ

Substituting value: 1 − 2(1 / 3) = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √3 tan θ = 3 sin θ

**Formula Used:** tan θ = sin θ / cos θ; sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc11deafb2a7cfc034ff24543842caa3fd4a7874f0338cd859f08efb76960a07.png] 

⇒ √3 (sin θ / cos θ) = 3 sin θ

⇒ √3 / cos θ = 3

⇒ cos θ = √3 / 3 = 1 / √3

⇒ cos² θ = (1 / √3)² = 1/3

⇒ From identity, sin² θ = 1 − cos² θ

⇒ sin² θ = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ Required value = sin² θ − cos² θ

⇒ Required value = 2/3 − 1/3 = 1/3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity

The primary identity relates sine and cosine as sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for any angle θ.

Double Angle Identity for Cosine

cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ. The expression in the question, sin²θ − cos²θ, is equivalent to −cos 2θ.

Tangent Property

The tangent ratio is defined as the quotient of sine and cosine: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.

Pythagoras Theorem in Trigonometry

For a right-angled triangle, Perpendicular² + Base² = Hypotenuse², which leads to the ratio identities.</p
